subject: Post-call recap & proposed evaluation sprint for PulseSight POC
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Lasker <tom.lasker@pulsesight.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed evaluation sprint for PulseSight POC

Tom — thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed sprint that should let you validate latency, throughput, and retrieval quality for the three production flows you described.

High-level success criteria (please confirm / add):
- 95th percentile generation latency <= 350ms for interactive queries (1-2 token/sec steady-state measurement).
- Semantic recall >= 92% on your labeled query set (we'll use the sample set you mentioned).
- End-to-end throughput >= 250 qps for batch ingestion window (nightly enrichment).
- No PII leakage on redacted fields; security questionnaire responses acceptable to your InfoSec.

Proposed sprint & milestones (owners):
- Week 0 — Kickoff & infra setup (Sep 27): Redwood infra lead (Ben) to provision sandbox, PulseSight to provide sample dataset and API credentials. Attachment: PS-MAP-v1.pdf
- Week 1 — Data ingest + baseline runs (Oct 4): Run baseline eval, smoke tests. Owner: Ben / PulseSight eng. Attachment: Eval-Checklist.xlsx
- Week 2 — Optimization & quantization trials (Oct 11): Measure cost/latency trade-offs and enable KV-prefix caching. Owner: Rafael / Ben
- Week 3 — QA sweep + run labeled queries (Oct 18): Calculate recall/precision vs. target. Owner: PulseSight / Redwood
- Final readout (Oct 22): Executive summary, decision rubric, next-step recommendations. Owner: Rafael / Tom

Immediate asks before kickoff:
1) Confirm the success criteria above or add any business KPIs you want measured.
2) Confirm availability for kickoff week (we propose Sep 27 or Sep 29).
3) Share a 1–2k sample of the target dataset and a representative query set (s3 link or temp credentials).
4) If needed, we'll route our MOU (mutual action plan) for signature — attached draft (PS-MAP-v1.pdf).

I've copied Marissa (CS lead) and Ben (infra) — Marissa will coordinate readouts and topline success metrics; Ben will run the sandbox configuration. I'll follow up with a more detailed workback and a security touchpoint.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
r.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0104

Attachments: PS-MAP-v1.pdf (mutual action plan), Eval-Checklist.xlsx (baseline tests)

From: Tom Lasker <tom.lasker@pulsesight.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed evaluation sprint for PulseSight POC

Rafael — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Dataset: the production set is ~80GB (compressed), but we can start with a 2k-row sample (JSONL) — I'll upload to the drive link you shared.
2) Compliance: we are SOC2 Type II in scope; we will need answers to three control areas up-front (data retention, tenant isolation for sandbox, logging/audit access). Can Marissa own the questionnaire?
3) Timing: Sep 27 is tight for our security team; Sep 29 kickoff works better.
4) Success KPI: add "99% availability for spike test windows" as an ops KPI during the batch ingestion run.

Also: can you confirm whether SSO/SCIM will be required for the short POC or if we can proceed with temp accounts? Our infra lead (eng@pulsesight.com) is on the thread and copied.

If Sep 29 is OK for Redwood, we'll treat Week 0 as a half-day pre-flight (access, samples) and schedule the full sandbox provisioning on Sep 30.

Best,
Tom
Head of Product, PulseSight
Tom Lasker | tom.lasker@pulsesight.com | +1 (415) 892-2210

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed evaluation sprint for PulseSight POC

Rafa — internal note before I loop Tom back. Suggested small tweaks: 
- Move kickoff to Sep 29 to match PulseSight availability. 
- Add a Week -0 security alignment (Sep 28): I can run the SOC2 control checklist; I'll attach the baseline Security-Q-A.docx and mark the three controls Tom called out.
- Ben should own sandbox provisioning and provide expected IAM roles + temp credential TTL (I'd recommend TTL 48 hours for initial keys).
- If they want SSO, we should treat SCIM as out-of-scope for the quick run but ask for a contact so we can scope for later.

I'll prepare the security touchpoint email and drop it into the shared Drive. Ben — can you confirm estimated time to stand up the sandbox (GPU-backed) and whether we can give them a limited audit log stream? If not, we should plan for an on-call window during Week 1 for live troubleshooting.

Thanks — Marissa
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: Security-Q-A.docx

From: Tom Lasker <tom.lasker@pulsesight.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, PulseSight Technical Team <eng@pulsesight.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed evaluation sprint for PulseSight POC

Rafael / Marissa / Ben — all good on our end. Confirming items below: 

- Kickoff: Sep 29 (half-day pre-flight) — PulseSight will provide the 2k sample by EOD Sep 23.
- Sandbox access: Temp accounts ok for now; our infra is comfortable with TTL 48h keys. No SSO for the POC run.
- Security: we'll review Security-Q-A.docx and come back with any follow-ups before Sep 28.
- KPI adjustment: we'll include the 99% availability spike window check in Week 1.
- Docs: I'll sign the MAP and return an executed copy once legal signs off.

Link to our escrow folder with the sample data and a short query set: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1z9PS-PulseSight-sample 

Looking forward to Sep 29 kickoff. Please send calendar invites for the workshop and weekly check-ins.

Thanks,
Tom
